chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: Lester Young and Herschel Evans: two camps of fans
summary: Greene says each tenor had his fans but he never saw bad feeling between them.

blocks.x: What about the feeling between Lester and Herschel. I mean, what was the nature of that? I mean, since they played, you know, totally different--
The two different styles?
Yeah.

Well, they -- each of them -- each had their own fan more or less. You know, musically each had their own fan, and when Lester would play, his group on his side was -- you know -- the Lester fan would (laugh)

Well, listen. I would like to get to something even more --
He hasn't finished telling about Herschel.
Oh, he's saying -- that's right.

Well, as I say, Hershel had his group. Lester had his group of fans, and when Lester would play, his group would, you know, cheer him on. And, then Hershel would play and his group would do the same. And, I think the audiences all over the country, more or less, was aware of this fact, and -- that was it.
But, I mean, did Hershel and Lester ever argue about how you should play the tenor, or anything like that? I mean, did they have any little jokes and feelings about that between them?
I never heard anything like that.
You didn't.
It was a funny thing -- you know what I mean -- everybody -- most people and most of the fans and people on the streets wondered how, you know. But, they got along well.
This is what -- that's why I say I want to get to something more subtle.

Yeah, you know. But as long as I've been there I've never noticed any of this feeling, you know -- bad feeling between the two of them, you know what I mean (laugh). They spoke to each other, you know, I mean, and --
They were two men who respected each other --

who had different worlds.
